- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 3–5%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 2–4% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–3% to reflect sentiment-driven sell-off.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is above 20-day moving average, forecast often stays above; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 days to align with reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overweights recent sentiment spikes; if sentiment peaks >0.8 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid sentiment-driven overcorrection.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
